programmes.d: 66 million years ago, an asteroid slammed into Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, causing a dinosaur mass extinction. With over 700,000 asteroids in space, what's in store for humanity and our planet if it happens again?
Heart disease is the number one cause of death worldwide, but there are researchers frantically working to change that.
The Tyrannosaurus Rex is known as the king of the dinosaurs, but how did its reigh begin? Meet Moros Intrepidus, a 180 lb., deer-sized ancestor to the T-Rex.
Wiped off the face of the Earth by humans nearly a century ago, geneticists are now working on ressurecting the enigmatic Tasmanian Tiger.
Thom meets a man with a superhuman sense of smell; George Aldrich is Nasa’s Chief Sniffer; employed to detect problems before they become a hazard in space.

Mt.Elgon is an 14,000 foot volcano in eastern Kenya. We propose a safari/ascent of the dormant volcano. Here’s the first kicker:High on the the flanks of the volcano is Kitum Cave – a cave created by the most unique form of erosion – Elephant Erosion

programmes.t: Angry Planet S2 - "By Camel to Timbuktu"
programmes.d: It is time for “Angry Planet” to do a serious desert episode. What better place to do it than this fabled city in the middle of the mighty Sahara Desert.

In June of next year we plan to intercept the Monsoon as it hits southern India and makes its way north along the western shore past Goa and Mumbai up to Delhi.This most famous of torrential rainy seasons drops as much as 40 feet of water.

programmes.t: Angry Planet S2 - "Java - Land of Fire"
programmes.d: The most notorious volcanic explosion in history came from the small island of Krakatoa, off the coast of Java. The tiny island was pulverized and the giant explosion was felt half way around the world. Java is at the heart of the Ring of Fire.
Hand powered tank, is that possible? Leonardo Da Vinci thought so. Today we will test this theory.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Radar Tech, Imperial War Museum, Land Mine Detection"
programmes.d: We have rare access to the German Aerospace Center outside Munich where scientists are using new forms of radar for surveillance and detecting land mines.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "RAF Station, Typhoon Squadron, The Flight Deck"
programmes.d: We're at Royal Air Force station Brize Norton, Oxfordshire, where we've been given an exclusive look at the RAF's ground-breaking, multi-role refuelling and transporter aircraft, the Voyager.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Targeting & Tracking, Navigation, Seagoing Drones"
programmes.d: We reveal an experimental sensor, monitoring and targeting system developed for troops by the UK's Defence Science and Technology Laboratory and Roke Manor Research. The iXblue Marins navigation black box guides navy ships.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "NATO Maritime Centre, No Shipping-No Shopping"
programmes.d: We visit NATO's Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation in La Spezia, Italy. We learn how the world's oceans are one of the last places that military technology can be hidden from prying eyes.

programmes.t: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Terrorist Threats, Sea Wasp Robot, Combat Medics"
programmes.d: With an increasing terrorist threat to ports and shipping, the Swedish manufacturer SAAB has developed the Sea Wasp, an under-water robot for detecting explosive devices.

programmes.t: Cold War: The Tech Race S1 - "Fuel for Destruction"
programmes.d: The atomic age introduces powerful rockets and nuclear energy, balancing technological advancement with threats like the Chernobyl disaster.

programmes.t: Cold War: The Tech Race S1 - "Golden Age of Science"
programmes.d: Military funding drives a boom in earth sciences and biological research, creating advanced weapons alongside deeper insights into our world.
Henry Ford's plan to build a giant factory in Michigan, covering 3.5million sq ft and including an aircraft production line half a mile in length.
The sabotaging efforts of Peugeot in Nazi-occupied France, where the bosses and workers cooperated with the Resistance to hinder the Nazis' use of military vehicles.
The story of America's `Liberty Ships', which were produced in incredible numbers and became known as the Model T Fords of the ocean.
The remarkable story of how Stalin's massive war factories were dismantled and moved east on one and half million railway trucks, to avoid being lost to the Nazis.
Artillery, the King of Battle, is explored as gunners train with powerful weapons and prepare for modern combat deployment.

programmes.t: Combat Forces S1 - "First Ten Combat Missions"
programmes.d: During the Vietnam War, the USAF learned most pilot losses happened in their first 10 missions, leading to intense training that saves lives.
At Fort Benning’s Army Combatives School, soldiers train in brutal hand-to-hand combat, learning real-world skills to fight and survive.
Stealthy diesel submarines challenge nuclear subs. Inside a NATO exercise, we explore why they’re so deadly in the Norwegian fjords.
In Colombia and Singapore, earthrise looks at sustainable forms of shelter.
Earthrise looks at methods of land restoration and conservation as human causes and climate change wreak havoc.
As the US no longer stands to be a global climate leader, China takes the mantle.
Earthrise sets off on a month-long journey around Antarctica to study the effects of climate change on the continent.
Earthrise assesses the depth of the crisis facing the world’s grasslands today, and explores some of the solutions that are being used to preserve them.

Throughout history, human society has run on trade. The innovations that allowed faster and more accurate oceanic travel revolutionized the world. New inventions now help people and goods move on the water faster for recreation and commerce.
Never in the history of humanity have so many of us been mobile. New innovations propel us into the world of self-driving cars and high-speed trains.

Growth in air transportation is set to soar, carrying over 10 billion passengers every year by 2050. To cope requires us to radically rethink aircraft design. Join us as we look into the world's most innovative research and development labs.

The most innovative area of human motion lies not on Earth, but with the exploration of space. Meet the private space entrepreneurs jostling to offer the tantalizing prospect of cheap, frequent travel beyond the atmosphere into Earth orbit.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S3 - "Who Owns Space?"
programmes.d: Join host Emily Calandrelli as we look at the futuristic plans of these companies, and the recent laws giving them permission.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S3 - "Stories from Space"
programmes.d: Host Emily Calandrelli visits each astronaut, including Story Musgrave, the only astronaut to fly aboard all five space shuttles, and Anna Fisher, one of the first American females to go into space.

programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S3 - "Second Annual Student Astronaut Contest"
programmes.d: Going aboard a Zero-G aircraft where they’ll experience microgravity with host, Emily Calandrelli.
Host Emily Calandrelli shows us robots that are leading the way, both to Mars, and other destinations in the future.

We take you flying in this classic Russian workhorse. Anthony gets hands-on with the revolutionary iPad tablet to show some of the most popular aviation tools available. A look at the future of commercial aviation… but who will be there to fly these things?

Kurtis takes us up in the aircraft that’s a crowd favorite wherever it he takes it. We spend some time with an ever-growing group of people who use their planes as campers and for one week a year, the tower at Oshkosh’s Wittman Regional Airport becomes the busiest on the planet.

programmes.t: The Aviators S3 - "WWII Pilot Training - T-6"
programmes.d: Kurtis earn his wings in a T-6 warbird at Stallion 51 Flight Operations in Kissimmee, FL!
